gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BestCarAudio.com tested a Kenwood eXcelon DMX908S with an iPhone 14 Pro on a QA403 analyzer and measured wireless CarPlay at 0.15072% THD+N and 56.62 dB SNR, against 0.01042% and 85.21 dB wired. That makes wireless about 14 times more distorted and about 29 dB noisier, with treble cut off near 17–17.5 kHz. ChatGPT gave wireless CarPlay as the main reason for every touchscreen pick.
standout_why: I read CarAudioNow's 'Best Car Stereos & Head Units (Tested)' guide, which ChatGPT cited and which says it was updated August 2026. Its only measured number is a boot time of 'roughly four to five seconds' for the Sony XAV-AX6000. It has no THD, noise or measured-power figures for any pick and does not compare wired and wireless CarPlay sound. I could not compare against Crutchfield: crutchfield.com/learn/best-car-stereo.html, its S-VCLheWFIcjk copy and crutchfield.ca/learn/best-touchscreen-car-stereos.html all returned HTTP 403, and curl was not permitted. Crutchfield's buying guides usually quote maker specs, but I have not confirmed these ones lack measurements.
decides: Wireless CarPlay was the selling point for the XAV-AX6000, DMH-WT6000NEX, iLX-W770 and DMX500S. BestCarAudio's test shows that connecting by cable gives much cleaner sound on that Kenwood: plugging in matters more than which head unit you pick. Shoppers who care about sound should plan to plug in, and wireless picks should be judged on convenience. Separately, BestCarAudio's bench numbers support ChatGPT naming the Sony XAV-9000ES best for sound quality. It measured 0.00458% THD+N and 5.365 V from the preamp, against the XAV-AX6000's 0.01138% and 5.101 V. Its built-in amp measured weaker, though: 17.6 W against 22.14 W per channel. So its advantage is for owners who add an external amplifier, not for running factory speakers off the head unit.
